speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your infant's recurrent stridor and wheezing, can you tell me if these symptoms occur specifically when the baby cries, feeds, or lies on their back?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The combination of inspiratory stridor that worsens with crying, feeding, and neck flexion (the sniffing position), along with feeding-related vomiting, is the classic clinical presentation for this condition.
